sources.entry: Dockge | Reactive manager for docker compose stacks

summary.one_liner: Dockge is a self-hosted, web-based manager for Docker Compose stacks that works directly on the compose.yaml files stored on disk.
summary.what_it_does: Dockge lets you create, edit, start, stop, restart, and delete Docker Compose stacks from a browser, and update their images. It includes an interactive editor for compose.yaml and a web terminal. Progress for pull, up, and down operations and terminal output are shown in real time. Stacks are plain files on the host, so they can still be managed with normal docker compose commands. The README also mentions a feature for converting docker run commands into compose.yaml, and multi-agent support (version 1.4.0) for managing stacks on several Docker hosts from one interface.
use_cases: manage docker compose stacks in a web UI
edit compose.yaml files in the browser
update docker images for compose stacks
convert docker run commands to compose files
manage stacks across multiple docker hosts
how_to_run: Open the web UI on port 5001
notable: Stacks stay as normal compose.yaml files on disk, so docker compose CLI still works on them
Real-time progress and terminal output for pull, up, and down
Multi-agent support to manage stacks on several Docker hosts (1.4.0)
Interactive compose.yaml generator and docker run to compose conversion
caveats: Windows is not supported yet (README says it will be later)
Debian/Raspbian Buster or older not supported
Focused on docker compose only; not a full Portainer replacement for networks or single containers
Stacks directory paths inside the container must match host paths, or data can be written to the wrong place
